text: {"features":[{"evidence":"Bachelor's degree / Master's degree / Doctoral degree","name":"relevant degree level","description":"Captures the highest explicitly stated technical degree, which is a stated qualification axis in the posting.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No degree is stated, or the letter relies only on practical experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"A bachelor's degree is stated."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"A master's degree is stated."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"A doctoral degree is stated."}]},{"evidence":"7 years and 6 production services","name":"production track record","description":"Captures how much directly relevant hands-on experience the letter claims in testing, maintaining, launching, and owning production software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Only minimal relevant depth is shown, such as just meeting the baseline or giving little evidence of repeated production ownership."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"A solid but moderate track record is shown, such as a few years of experience or several launched services."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"A strong track record is shown, with multiple years and repeated production launches or ownership."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"An extensive track record is shown, combining multi-year experience with many launched services and clear evidence of sustained production work."}]},{"evidence":"Python is production-grade","name":"Python depth","description":"Captures how concretely and credibly the letter shows Python as a serious working language for the role's automation and agent work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No Python experience is stated."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Python is mentioned only briefly or as light scripting."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Python is described as a regular language for tooling, automation, prototypes, or internal services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Python is positioned as production-strength, with clear responsibility for robust services, analysis layers, or core automation used by others."}]},{"evidence":"shipping LLM-backed features and hardening them","name":"AI deployment experience","description":"Captures whether the letter shows real experience applying AI systems in production rather than only interest in them.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No AI experience is stated."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"AI is mentioned vaguely or aspirationally, without shipped work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states that AI or LLM-backed features were built and shipped in production."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows shipped AI systems plus reliability work such as evaluation, hardening, trustworthiness, or handling failure modes."}]},{"evidence":"threat modeling and code review","name":"security review depth","description":"Captures the depth of direct security assessment work the applicant claims on real systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No security assessment experience is stated."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Security review is mentioned in broad terms, with little method or scope."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly describes structured assessment work such as threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, or code review for vulnerabilities."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows structured assessments plus engineering follow-through such as validating fixes, verifying remediation, or treating assessments as design work."}]},{"evidence":"automated the intake and triage of vulnerability reports","name":"vulnerability triage automation","description":"Captures whether the letter shows direct experience automating the vulnerability-handling workflow central to this job.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter expresses interest in reducing security toil but gives no concrete triage system example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter describes building automation for intake, classification, routing, deduplication, or prioritization of vulnerability reports."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes such automation and also explains meaningful operational effect, such as making a queue self-serve or returning expert time to the team."}]},{"evidence":"Python agents with Go guardrails","name":"agent architecture experience","description":"Captures how directly the letter matches the role's agent-building work with concrete design experience spanning agents and supporting infrastructure.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No agentic or multi-agent system design is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Agents or AI tooling are mentioned only at a high level, without architecture details."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter describes building agentic systems with a clear split between Go back-end systems and Python agents."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes end-to-end agentic architecture with explicit attention to autonomy, permissions, constraints, guardrails, or auditability."}]},{"evidence":"turned brute-force correlation into streaming computation","name":"algorithmic sophistication","description":"Captures how strongly the letter demonstrates data-structures-and-algorithms skill through concrete engineering examples.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No data structures or algorithm work is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Algorithmic strength is claimed only generically, with no example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"At least one concrete example is given of using a better structure or algorithm to improve a system."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"A technically specific, high-leverage example is given that shows sophisticated algorithmic redesign on an important path or hard systems problem."}]},{"evidence":"maintainer of an open-source project used beyond my own team","name":"open-source ownership","description":"Captures the degree to which the letter shows responsibility for external codebases and users, beyond private internal work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No open-source activity is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions occasional patches or limited upstream contributions."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows regular contribution or maintenance of a smaller project."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows maintainer-level ownership with external users, reviews, releases, or community support responsibilities."}]},{"evidence":"replicated cache with proper failover","name":"side-project rigor","description":"Captures whether personal projects in the letter signal technical curiosity and willingness to tackle difficult engineering problems outside assigned work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No personal technical project is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"A modest side project is mentioned, mainly signaling steady practice rather than technical difficulty."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"A substantive personal project is described with meaningful engineering depth."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"An ambitious side project is described that was explicitly chosen for hard edge cases, distributed-systems semantics, or other unforgiving technical challenges."}]},{"evidence":"near-top capture-the-flag finishes","name":"external security commitment","description":"Captures security seriousness shown through recurring practice or credentials outside ordinary product-engineering duties.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification."}]},{"evidence":"impact compounds across all of Google","name":"platform leverage mindset","description":"Captures how clearly the letter wants this role for its central platform effect rather than as a generic security job.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The motivation is generic, with no platform or multiplier rationale."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions scale or impact broadly, but not in a specific platform way."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter explicitly values foundational or Core work whose benefits spread across many teams."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter gives a nuanced explanation of multiplier effects such as capacity creation, fleet-wide protection, or centralized improvements inherited downstream."}]},{"evidence":"defaults, not documents","name":"secure-defaults mindset","description":"Captures whether the letter presents security as something embedded into developer workflows and default behaviors rather than imposed afterward.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No clear philosophy is given for how security should interact with product teams."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions secure development or helping teams only in generic terms."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter explicitly emphasizes embedding best practices into the lifecycle or assisting developers proactively."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter gives a crisp, memorable philosophy about secure defaults, low-friction developer support, or avoiding after-the-fact policing."}]},{"evidence":"memorable opening hook versus checklist fragments","name":"narrative structure","description":"Captures how well the letter turns qualifications into a persuasive, role-specific story rather than a disconnected list.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter reads mainly as fragments, bullet-like assertions, or a checklist of qualifications."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter is understandable but mostly lists claims with limited progression or synthesis."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter has a coherent progression from motivation to evidence to fit."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is especially well-shaped, using memorable framing and smooth transitions to reinforce fit."}]},{"evidence":"repeated misspellings throughout","name":"proofreading discipline","description":"Captures the surface-level care of the letter as shown by spelling and typographical control.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent noticeable errors repeatedly interrupt reading."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Several clear errors are present, though the overall meaning remains easy to follow."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Only a few minor errors are present."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is essentially clean, with little or no visible proofreading lapse."}]},{"evidence":"returned expert hours to the team","name":"outcome specificity","description":"Captures whether the letter substantiates its capabilities with concrete results, scope, or operational effect rather than generic assertions.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Claims are mostly broad and unbacked by specific examples or results."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"At least one specific task or tool is mentioned, but the problem, method, or result is thinly described."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Several concrete examples show what was built or improved."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Multiple role-relevant claims are backed by specific problems, actions, and outcomes or measurable operational effect."}]}]}
